text: Know the enemy and know yourself; in a hundred battles you will never be in peril.
source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War, III

text: A journey of a thousand li begins with a single step.
source: Laozi, Dao De Jing, 64

text: It is possible to commit no mistakes and still lose. That is not a weakness. That is life.
source: Jean-Luc Picard, Star Trek: The Next Generation, 'Peak Performance'

text: No one here is exactly what he appears.
source: G'Kar, Babylon 5, 'The Gathering'

text: Faith manages.
source: Brother Theo, Babylon 5, 'The Paragon of Animals'

text: Logic is the beginning of wisdom, not the end.
source: Spock, Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country

text: I don't believe in the no-win scenario.
source: James T. Kirk, Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

text: Time is the fire in which we burn.
source: Soran, Star Trek: Generations

text: I can live with it.
source: Benjamin Sisko, Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, 'In the Pale Moonlight'

text: Supreme excellence consists in breaking the enemy's resistance without fighting.
source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War, III

text: Knowing others is intelligence; knowing yourself is true wisdom.
source: Laozi, Dao De Jing, 33

text: The first duty of every Starfleet officer is to the truth — whether it be scientific truth, historical truth, or personal truth.
source: Jean-Luc Picard, Star Trek: The Next Generation, 'The First Duty'

text: The needs of the many outweigh the needs of the few.
source: Spock, Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan

text: I lied. I cheated. I bribed men to cover the crimes of other men. I am an accessory to murder. But the most damning thing of all, I think I can live with it.
source: Benjamin Sisko, Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, 'In the Pale Moonlight'

text: All warfare is based on deception.
source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War, I

text: The soft overcomes the hard; the gentle overcomes the rigid.
source: Laozi, Dao De Jing, 43

text: Live now; make now always the most precious time. Now will never come again.
source: Jean-Luc Picard, Star Trek: The Next Generation, 'The Inner Light'

text: It's easy to be a saint in paradise.
source: Benjamin Sisko, Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, 'The Maquis, Part II'

text: The victorious strategist only seeks battle after the victory has been won, whereas he who is destined to defeat first fights and afterwards looks for victory.
source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War, IV

text: To know that you do not know is the best. To think you know when you do not is a disease.
source: Laozi, Dao De Jing, 71

text: The first link in the chain of circumstances is the one that is most difficult to break.
source: Jean-Luc Picard, Star Trek: The Next Generation, 'Tapestry'

text: If you want to assassinate a man, you don't need a Starfleet officer to do it. You need a Romulan.
source: Benjamin Sisko, Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, 'In the Pale Moonlight'

text: He who knows when he can fight and when he cannot will be victorious.
source: Sun Tzu, The Art of War, III

text: When the work is done, the people all say: we did it ourselves.
source: Laozi, Dao De Jing, 17

text: There are times, sir, when men of good conscience cannot blindly follow orders.
source: Jean-Luc Picard, Star Trek: The Next Generation, 'The Drumhead'

text: In the end, a man has to live with his choices.
source: Benjamin Sisko, Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, 'In the Pale Moonlight'

text: Nothing under heaven is softer or more yielding than water, yet nothing can resist it.
source: Laozi, Dao De Jing, 78

text: Villains who twirl their moustaches are easy to spot. Those who clothe themselves in good deeds are well camouflaged.
source: Jean-Luc Picard, Star Trek: The Next Generation, 'The Drumhead'

text: He who does not trust enough will not be trusted.
source: Laozi, Dao De Jing, 17

text: The road from legitimate suspicion to rampant paranoia is very much shorter than we think.
source: Jean-Luc Picard, Star Trek: The Next Generation, 'The Drumhead'
